To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The prevalence of mental illness in the general community is 1 in 5.
Psychiatric symptoms in the mentally retarded can be assessed in the same manner as in the non-retarded, but the process is more challenging and the diagnosis is less clear-cut.
(i) the prevalence of psychiatric disorders among mentally retarded persons is high, and (ii) these psychiatric disorders are associated with significant morbidity, mortality and service costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and management of mental health problems in mentally retarded individuals, particularly in those with Down syndrome.
understanding and preventing the emotional and behavioural disorders of the mentally retarded.
the development and evaluation of a clinical assessment tool for psychiatric symptoms in mentally retarded persons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
psychiatric disorders are common, serious and under-identified in the mentally retarded, and that a psychiatric diagnosis can be made in the majority of cases.
mentally retarded individuals with emotional and behavioural disturbance are seriously underserved by psychiatrists.
mentally retarded persons are at risk of psychiatric disorders, but are not more vulnerable to psychopathology than non-mentally retarded individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the psychiatric disorders of mentally retarded individuals are not caused by the retardation itself, but by a combination of biological, psychological and social factors which increase their vulnerability.

we have developed a model for psychiatric assessment of mentally handicapped persons which can be applied to the assessment of psychiatric symptoms and which is applicable in a range of clinical settings.
the mentally retarded individual with psychiatric symptoms is best managed within a multidisciplinary team approach, with the psychiatrist as a key player in the management process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mentally retarded are not a homogeneous group.
the psychiatric assessment of a mentally retarded patient is not a simple process.
psychiatric assessment of mentally handicapped individuals can be undertaken by psychiatrists with a good understanding of the principles and methods involved.
